text:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a priming probe on the meta-judge during the new model bring-up. seeing tie-break churn when we toggle "rationale" priming vs none. :thinking:
liam: link? which model + runner config?
maya: using meta-judge-v2 on the new quantized model (q4_0). runner config attached below. small sample (~2k pairs).
liam: can you paste the config? want to reproduce locally.
maya: sure:
```json
{
  "judge_model": "meta-judge-v2",
  "priming": "rationale",
  "seed": 42,
  "tie_breaker": "random_sampling",
  "batch_size": 32
}
```
anita: interesting. what metric are you using to decide ties? majority? confidence delta?
maya: default is majority; if tied we do random_sampling with seed. but when priming changes, majority flips ~6% of cases. disagreement rate jumps from 11% -> 18% with rationale priming.
oliver: 6% swing is non-trivial. did you compute Cohen's kappa or Krippendorff alpha? might indicate inconsistency not just more ties.
maya: ran kappa quick: 0.71 -> 0.59. Krippendorff down similarly. WARN in logs:
```
WARN: disagreement rate 0.18 -> exceeds threshold 0.12
```
sara: could be prompt leakage / priming bias. did you check for prompt contamination (e.g., model output contains training data that hints at a particular label)? :eyes:
liam: also check sampling nondeterminism across runner shards. eval-runner-bot, did you see flaky seeds on that job?
eval-runner-bot: job 1789123001 completed. artifacts: gs://redwood-evals/1789123001/{preds,logs}. No deterministic mismatch detected across two replays (seed 42).
liam: hm. so not runner RNG. maybe the judge's calibration shifts when rationale token overhead changes confidence estimates.
anita: proposal: switch tie-breaker to deterministic confidence-mean (pick label with highest mean confidence across samples) for the CI baseline, and keep random_sampling only for exploratory runs. lower flakiness in test history?
maya: agree. quick AB: use tie_breaker = "highest_avg_confidence" and rerun 1000 pairs.
oliver: also document metric: report (majority_accuracy, mean_confidence_gap, cohen_kappa). add per-priming breakdown to dashboard.
sara: if bias is the issue, we should add a parity test: stratify by source domain (docs, chat, email) and surface per-stratum disagreement.
liam: CI note — recent judge model bump triggered a red on evals last week. ops: the CI wiring treats any >0.05 absolute delta in majority_accuracy as fail. maybe too tight for priming-sensitive configs.
maya: yeah that rule caught a lot of noisy failures. suggest adding a rubric-level tolerance for "primed_judges" path. e.g., widen threshold to 0.08 if priming != "none".
anita: I worry about masking real regressions. instead, keep strict CI but require a human sign-off checkbox on PRs that change judge priming or tie-breaker behavior.
liam: good compromise. automation: if CI flags and diff <0.08 and priming changed, create a "judge-review" issue with perf plot.
ci-bot: CREATED issue #eval-judge-review-178912 — /evals/reports/1789123001. ping @maya @liam for triage.
maya: thanks. next steps for me: rerun with deterministic tie-breaker, produce per-stratum breakdown, and add a short note on priming artifacts. will paste findings here.
oliver: for long-term, we should add a small synthetic suite where we control gold rationale vs no-rationale to quantify bias introduced by prompting. that will live in the judge-e2e folder.
sara: also add a metric for "tie_entropy" — how often ties are low-confidence vs high-confidence. could indicate when ties actually matter.
maya: cool. rerun kicked off: job 1789124002. I'll post results when finished. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: job 1789124002 queued. artifacts will be available in ~30m.
liam: awesome. small nit: can we make runner logs include `priming` in the job metadata label so filtering in BigQuery is easier?
maya: done on the rerun.
eval-runner-bot: job 1789124002 finished. summary:
- majority_accuracy delta (rationale vs none): 0.036
- disagreement rate (rationale): 0.162
- cohen_kappa: 0.62
- tie_breaker=highest_avg_confidence reduced stochastic flips by ~40%
link: https://console.redwood/evals/1789124002
anita: that's promising. can you upload a quick dashboard screenshot to the issue?
maya: uploaded. PR to builder-configs to add deterministic tie-breaker to CI baseline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/builder-configs/pull/1123
liam: leaving a short TODO: 1) add priming-aware CI rule 2) add stratified parity checks 3) add synthetic rationale suite 4) document tie-breakers in judge-runner README.
sara: and 5) brainstorm non-deterministic tie-break fallback policy: prefer model variant with higher calibration score.
maya: thanks team. will follow up with a small RFC next week for the judge rubric changes. :wave:
